apparatus_caveat: Only these complete bounded prayer selections have been collated; this is not a full Ordinary or full missal diff. Printed 1606 and 1657 dates are witness dates, not proof of each variant’s introduction. The 1655 mandate and cited general chapters are separate contextual evidence. Long s, display initials, nasal abbreviations and line wraps are normalized as declared in the owning artifacts; source accents, u/v, ligatures, abbreviations and short endings otherwise remain. Spoken blocks and rubric positions remain recoverable; the 1657 (vel meis) is a printed alternative, not simultaneous speech. No immediate predecessor relationship, complete Romanization, or modern liturgical authorization is inferred.
basis: The complete Orate invitation and response dialogue in each identified edition share the invitation to pray for acceptance of the sacrifice. The 1606 Dominus sit in corde tuo response differs from the 1657 Suscipiat Dominus; the later printed alternative and final priestly Amen remain explicit. This is alignment of the same liturgical function, not a claim that the two response compositions are identical.

unified_diff:
--- left/cistercian-1606-latin-ordinary
+++ right/cistercian-1657-latin-ordinary
@@ -1,5 +1,3 @@
-Oráte, fratres, pro me peccatóre:
-vt meum páriter ac vestrum in conspéctu Dómini acceptábile fiat sacrifícium.
-Dóminus sit in corde tuo & in lábiis tuis, suscipiátque de mánibus tuis sacrifícium istud:
-& oratiónes tuæ ascéndant in memóriam ante Deum pro nostra, & totíus pópuli salúte.
+Oráte fratres, vt meum ac vestrum sacrifícium acceptábile fiat apud Deum patrem omnipoténtem.
+Suscípiat Dóminus sacrifícium de mánibus tuis (vel meis) ad laudem & glóriam nóminis sui, ad vtilitátem quoque nostram, totiúsque Ecclésiæ suæ sanctæ.
 Amen.
